newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Wheat Board endorses new structure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Wheat Board endorses new structure.

text.p: The chairman of the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), Trevor Flugge, has endorsed the new structure agreed on for the AWB by Grains Council of Australia (GCA).
"It's a sound basis for the AWB to become fully commercial in this increasingly competitive world grain market," he said.
The new structure for the AWB has been agreed on by a working group involving GCA, the AWB and the federal Department of Primary Industries and Energy (DPIE).

The model retains the AWB's single desk monopoly, grower ownership and control, an adequate capital base for maintaining the system of harvest payments, commercial flexibility and industry self-determination, a joint statement by AWB, GCA and DPIE said.
The new AWB model is based on A and B class shares and involves the creation of separate AWB subsidiaries to conduct wheat pooling and commercial activities under a holding company structure.
One class A share would be issued to each wheat grower at nominal value. Class A shareholders would vote for a majority of the directors of the holding company on a one-grower one-vote basis.

B class shares would be issued in a conversion of equity in the grower levy-funded Wheat Industry Fund in 1999. Consideration would be given to listing the B class shares on the Australian Stock Exchange after the review of the AWB's single export desk in year 2000, the statement said.
The AWB package would be presented to the Minister for Primary Industries and Energy as part of a five-year plan outlining the industry's future direction, the statement said.
The agreement settles a longstanding dispute in the Australian grains industry over the future structure of the Australian Wheat Board, which is being commercialised by the Australian government.
GCA in the past had insisted on a trust fund arrangement for the new AWB.
